headline: Sequence models decode antibody, TCR, and peptide-HLA immune recognition
label: Immune Receptor Sequence Modeling
summary: Pretrained and interpretable sequence models now span antibody, TCR, and peptide-HLA recognition, with generative and longitudinal extensions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is pretrained or interpretable sequence modeling of immune recognition. HCAbLM is pretrained on 31.8 million fully human heavy-chain-only antibody sequences and learns region-selective sequence priors. OmniTCR, a 113M-parameter autoregressive model trained on 328M immune-sequence records, jointly models TCR recognition prediction and conditional sequence generation. LAMINA, with 4.7M parameters, matches state-of-the-art peptide-HLA affinity prediction and is reported to learn binding energetics and structure emergently. DeepAir-Cov19 (AUC 0.94) identifies SARS-CoV-2-specific TCRs and tracks post-vaccination TCR dynamics tied to antibody levels. PAbFold applies localColabFold/AlphaFold2 to linear antibody epitope prediction. What is new is joint interpretability, generation, and longitudinal repertoire tracking within immune-receptor models, while the items do not report explicit physical-force coupling or inference-time conformational control.
